title: Ordered & Description Lists 🔢
description: Numbered lists, custom start values, and key‑value definitions with `<dl>`.

slides.title: Ordered Lists (`<ol>`) 1️⃣2️⃣3️⃣
slides.content:
# Steps That Need Order When the sequence matters – like a recipe or a ranking – use an **ordered list**. Same `
  • ` items, but wrapped in `
      `. ```html
      1. Preheat oven to 180°C
      2. Mix ingredients
      3. Bake for 25 minutes
      ``` Browser automatically numbers the items 1, 2, 3…

slides.title: Customising Ordered Lists 🎛️
slides.content:
# Change Number Style and Start Attributes on `
    `: - `type` – `"1"` (numbers, default), `"A"` uppercase letters, `"a"` lowercase, `"I"` Roman numerals, `"i"` lowercase Roman. - `start` – a number to start counting from (e.g., `start="5"`). - `reversed` – reverses the order (e.g., 3, 2, 1). ```html
    1. Step D
    2. Step E
    ``` This list will show D, E (starting at 4, so D=4, E=5).

quizData.question: Which attribute makes an ordered list display Roman numerals?
quizData.explanation: The `type` attribute with value `I` (uppercase i) yields uppercase Roman numerals.

slides.title: A Countdown with `reversed`
slides.codeSnippet:
Top 3 Movies of 2025

  1. The Star Builder
  2. Quantum Echo
  3. Into the Depths

slides.title: Description Lists (`<dl>`) 📖
slides.content:
# Terms and Definitions

A **description list** pairs terms (`<dt>`) with descriptions (`<dd>`). Great for glossaries, metadata, or FAQ.

```html
<dl>
  <dt>HTML</dt>
  <dd>HyperText Markup Language – the structure of web pages.</dd>
  <dt>CSS</dt>
  <dd>Cascading Style Sheets – controls presentation.</dd>
</dl>
```
You can have multiple `<dd>` for one `<dt>`, or vice versa, though it's less common.

quizData.question: A `<dt>` must always be followed by exactly one `<dd>`.
quizData.explanation: You can have multiple `<dd>` elements for one term, or even group several `<dt>`/`<dd>` pairs inside one `<dl>`.

slides.title: A Simple FAQ Section
slides.content: Using description lists for questions and answers:
slides.codeSnippet:
<dl>
  <dt>What is Progly?</dt>
  <dd>A mobile app that teaches coding through bite‑sized lessons.</dd>
  <dt>Is it free?</dt>
  <dd>Yes! Core lessons are free; advanced content is premium.</dd>
</dl>
